title: Breaker rating vs. conductor ampacity
citation: CEC Rule 14-104 / Table 2 [PLACEHOLDER — verify actual clause]
requirement: Each branch circuit overcurrent device rating must not exceed the allowable ampacity of the conductor it protects (with the standard next-size-up allowances).

title: Continuous load sizing allowance
requirement: Conductors and overcurrent devices serving continuous loads must be sized for at least 125% of the continuous load current.

title: Service/feeder load calculation present
requirement: The submission must include a calculated load for the service or feeder showing the demand used to select the service size.

title: Service size adequate for calculated load
requirement: The rated ampacity of the service or feeder must be equal to or greater than the calculated demand load.

title: Bonding conductor sizing and presence
citation: CEC Rule 10-614 / Table 16 [PLACEHOLDER — verify actual clause]
requirement: A bonding conductor must be shown for each feeder/branch circuit and sized from the rating of the largest overcurrent device in the run.

title: Grounding electrode / system grounding detail
requirement: The submission must include a grounding detail identifying the grounding electrode and the grounding conductor size.

title: Working space in front of equipment
requirement: A minimum 1 m working space must be shown in front of panelboards and other equipment likely to require examination while energized.

title: Panelboard not installed in prohibited location
requirement: Panelboards must not be located in bathrooms, clothes closets, stairways or similar restricted locations.

title: Arc-flash / shock hazard labelling
citation: CSA Z462 / CEC Rule 2-306 [PLACEHOLDER — verify actual clause]
requirement: Equipment likely to be worked on while energized must be identified with an arc-flash and shock hazard warning label.

title: Circuit directory / panel schedule legibility
requirement: Each panelboard must have a legible circuit directory identifying the load served by every circuit.

title: GFCI protection for wet/damp and outdoor receptacles
requirement: Receptacles outdoors, in bathrooms, and within 1.5 m of sinks must be GFCI (Class A) protected.

title: AFCI protection for dwelling branch circuits
requirement: Branch circuits supplying receptacles in dwelling units must have arc-fault protection unless a listed exception applies.

title: Overcurrent device interrupting rating vs. available fault current
requirement: The interrupting rating of overcurrent devices must be at least the available fault current at the point of installation, and the available fault current must be stated.

title: Disconnecting means identified and accessible
requirement: A readily accessible disconnecting means must be shown and identified for the service and for each piece of fixed equipment.

title: Equipment certification / approval marking
requirement: All electrical equipment shown must be certified/approved for use in Canada, with the certification mark or special-inspection path identified.
